No directly matched ablation found establishing that averaging SASRec’s last several contextual states beats its final state. Each causal state already encodes its preceding prefix; averaging recent states therefore mixes overlapping histories and predictions trained for different next-item targets, rather than isolating recent items. This is an architectural inference. [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781) provides supporting attention visualizations: sparse Beauty emphasizes recency; dense ML-1M uses longer history; upper layers attend more locally, plausibly because lower layers already incorporate distant information.

Recent item-embedding pooling has stronger direct evidence. [HAM, §§6.1–6.6](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10034966/) finds mean pooling superior to max pooling across six datasets and competitive against learned HGN gates. Removing its explicit recent-item term hurts Books and ML-1M, but slightly improves CDs: recency benefits are dataset-dependent. [HGN, Table 4](https://arxiv.org/html/1906.09217) compares feature/instance gates, average/max pooling, and item–item scoring. On Comics, combining both gates with average pooling gives Recall@10 0.1635 versus 0.1555 for feature gating alone; adding item–item scoring reaches 0.1743. These support complementary preference components, without proving contextual-state averaging helps.

Oversmoothing warrants a separate control. [BSARec, Table 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2312.10325v2) reports Beauty HR@20 0.1373 with combined attention/frequency modeling versus 0.1265 with attention alone; this supports preserving high-frequency information, not additional averaging. Suggested controls: final state; last-k contextual mean; last-k raw embedding mean; fixed versus learned mixtures with the final state; recent versus equally sized older-state windows. Match training/readout, padding masks, normalization and tuning budgets. Measure validation HR@10 alongside state cosine similarity and effective rank: distinguish recency gains from generic smoothing or redundant prefix aggregation.
